operations.specification: Create a new guest account by validating email format, checking email uniqueness against the guests table, hashing the password using bcrypt, and creating a new guest record with the provided email, hashed password, and display_name. After successful account creation, generate a JWT session token by creating a record in the guest_sessions table with access_token and refresh_token derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint. Return the newly created guest account information with the authentication token.
operations.description:
User Registration - This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to create a new guest account in the multi-user todo application by providing their email address, password, and display name. The email address is validated for proper format using standard email validation patterns and must be unique across all guest accounts in the multi_user_todo_app_guests table. If the email format is invalid or the email is already registered, the request is rejected with an appropriate error.

The password is required and must be securely hashed using bcrypt before being stored in the password field of the guest record. Upon successful account creation, the system automatically generates a JWT session by creating an entry in the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table with both access_token and refresh_token values derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint information. This session enables the newly registered guest to perform authenticated operations immediately after registration.

The display_name becomes the guest's visible identifier across the application and is stored in the display_name field. This endpoint returns the complete guest account information including the generated authentication token, allowing the client to immediately begin using the authenticated features of the application without a separate login step.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials for creating a new guest account

responseBody.description: Authenticated guest account with session token

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the provided refresh token by looking up the corresponding guest_sessions record in the database using the refresh_token field. If the token is valid and not expired, generate a new access_token by creating a new session record with a fresh access_token and refresh_token pair derived from the guest_id and device fingerprint. Invalidate the old refresh token to prevent replay attacks. Return the new access token to the client.
operations.description:
Token Refresh - This endpoint allows guests to renew their expired JWT session tokens without requiring re-authentication. Guests receive both access_token and refresh_token during registration via the join operation. The refresh_token is used to obtain new access tokens when the original access token expires.

The system validates the refresh token by querying the multi_user_todo_app_guest_sessions table for a matching refresh_token record. The token must be valid (not expired, not previously invalidated) and associated with an active guest account in the multi_user_todo_app_guests table. If the token is invalid, expired, or has been used, the refresh request is rejected.

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access_token and refresh_token pair by creating a new guest_sessions record. The old refresh token is invalidated to prevent replay attacks. This ensures that each refresh token can only be used once, maintaining the security of the session. The client receives the new access token and should replace the old one for subsequent authenticated requests.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing the guest session

responseBody.description: New session token for the guest

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Create new member account with email, password, and display name. Verify email format and uniqueness, hash password using bcrypt before storing, create member record with createdAt timestamp, generate JWT session tokens (access and refresh) stored in multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions, return member profile and authorization tokens. Password must meet minimum complexity requirements. Return 409 Conflict if email already registered.
operations.description:
Registration endpoint for new member accounts in the multi-user todo application. This operation creates a new authenticated user account using email address and password credentials, along with an optional display name for profile identification.

The database schema multi_user_todo_app_members stores member information with fields: email for unique identification and login, password for credential validation (stored as hash), displayName for display purposes, createdAt timestamp automatically set when account is created, and updatedAt timestamp updated on profile modifications.

Upon successful registration, the system generates JWT session tokens (access_token and refresh_token) stored in the multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table, enabling immediate authenticated access to the member's private todo resources without requiring a separate login step.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials and profile information for new member account

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and initial member profile after successful registration

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate member using email and password credentials. Query multi_user_todo_app_members by email, validate password hash matches stored value, verify account exists and is active. Upon successful authentication, revoke existing refresh tokens and generate new JWT access and refresh tokens stored in multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions. Return member profile with authorization tokens. Return 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials or non-existent account.
operations.description:
Login endpoint for member account authentication using email and password credentials. This operation validates the member's credentials against the stored values in the multi_user_todo_app_members table and issues JWT session tokens for authenticated API access.

The database schema multi_user_todo_app_members contains the email field for unique user identification and the password field for credential storage (hashed using bcrypt). When a member provides their email and password, the system queries for a matching record, verifies the password hash, and upon validation success, creates new session tokens.

The multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table stores JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) with timestamps and device identifiers. Upon successful login, any existing session tokens for that member are invalidated to prevent concurrent session conflicts, ensuring fresh tokens are issued for the new authenticated session.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for member account authentication

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and member profile after successful authentication

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh expired access token using valid refresh token. Query multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions for matching refresh_token, validate token expiration, member_id, and device_fingerprint match stored values. Upon validation success, generate new access token with extended expiration (1 hour) and new refresh token (7 days), store both in sessions table, invalidate old tokens, and return new authorization tokens. Return 401 Unauthorized for invalid, expired, or mismatched refresh tokens.
operations.description:
Token refresh endpoint for renewing expired JWT access tokens without re-authentication. This operation allows members to obtain new access tokens using a valid refresh token from the multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table, eliminating the need to re-enter credentials.

The multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table contains session records with access_token, refresh_token, member_id, device_fingerprint, created_at, and expires_at fields. The system validates that the provided refresh_token matches a stored session record, verifies the member_id and device_fingerprint match the original session, and checks that the token has not expired.

Upon successful validation, the system generates new JWT tokens (access_token with 1-hour expiration, refresh_token with 7-day expiration), stores them in the sessions table, and invalidates the old refresh token to prevent token reuse. This enables seamless authentication without requiring members to log in again.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authorization tokens

responseBody.description: New authorization tokens after successful refresh

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Update the current authenticated user's display name in their profile.

This operation allows a member user to modify their display name, which is the name that identifies them within the multi-user todo application. The display name is shown throughout the system to identify the user and can be updated at any time through their profile settings.

The request must include a valid Bearer authentication token in the Authorization header. Only the profile owner can update their own display name; cross-user profile access is strictly prohibited for privacy reasons. Users cannot set their display name to an empty value or a value containing only whitespace.

Display name changes are immediately reflected in the user's profile and are permanent. The system validates that the new display name contains at least one character before persisting the update.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Authenticate the request using Bearer token from Authorization header.

Validate the token belongs to an active member session.

Extract the member_id from the authenticated session.

Parse the request body to extract the displayName field.

Validate displayName is not empty and not whitespace-only.

Validate displayName does not conflict with existing users.

Execute UPDATE query on multi_user_todo_app_members table:
  - Set displayName = new value
  - Set updatedAt = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  - WHERE member_id = authenticated_member_id

Return the updated profile record with id, displayName, and updatedAt.

If authentication fails, return 401 Unauthorized.
If validation fails, return 400 Bad Request with specific error.
If update fails, return 500 Internal Server Error.

responseBody.description: The updated user profile containing the new display name

requestBody.description: Profile update request containing the new display name

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated member's active sessions.

This operation allows users to view all their login sessions across devices, including session metadata such as device identifier, client IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamps. Sessions are used for authentication tracking and security auditing.

Each session represents a single authenticated device or browser combination. The system supports multiple concurrent sessions per member, enabling users to log in from multiple devices simultaneously (e.g., mobile phone, desktop, tablet).

The operation supports filtering by session status (active/expired), date range for session creation, and device identifier patterns. Results are paginated to handle large session histories efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table for the authenticated member.

Filtering criteria:
- Filter by session status: active (expired_at >= current time) or expired
- Filter by creation date range: created_at between start and end
- Filter by device_id pattern match (partial matching)
- Filter by IP address pattern match

Pagination:
- Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination
- Default page size: 10, maximum: 100
- Sort by created_at descending (newest sessions first)

Join requirements:
- No joins required - all session data is in the member_sessions table
- Belongs to member table but member details not needed for this operation

Security:
- Filter by authenticated member's ID (multi_user_todo_app_member_id)
- Users can only view their own sessions
- Return summary information (hide sensitive token data)

Edge cases:
- Return empty array if no sessions exist
- Handle expired_at null or past timestamps correctly
- Validate pagination parameters (min 1, max 100)

requestBody.description: Session listing filter criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific authentication session for the authenticated member from the multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table.

This operation returns metadata about a member's login session including the session creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, connection information (IP address, browser path, referrer source), and session status. The session data is used for security auditing, session management, and allowing members to monitor their active logins across different devices.

The session owner (the member who created this session) is the only authorized actor who can view this session's details. Attempting to access another member's session results in an authorization error. This enforces the privacy policy that authentication metadata is isolated to each user account. Each session is linked to a member through the multi_user_todo_app_member_id foreign key.

The response includes the session's unique identifier, the member's ID, the IP address from the original request, the URL path (href) that was accessed during login, the referrer header value, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. Note that sensitive token values (access_token, refresh_token) are stored as hashes and are not returned in the API response for security reasons.

Sessions are managed automatically through the authentication system. This endpoint provides read-only access to session metadata for purposes such as displaying active sessions in the user interface, identifying suspicious login activity, or preparing for session termination via the logout operation. Sessions are append-only audit records that are never modified after creation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the requesting user is authenticated (has valid session token).
2. Extract sessionId from path parameter and validate it is a valid UUID format.
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions table for record with matching id.
4. Verify that the retrieved session belongs to the authenticated member (multi_user_todo_app_member_id == authenticated_user_id).
5. If session not found, return 404 Not Found error.
6. If session does not belong to authenticated user, return 403 Forbidden error.
7. Return session metadata (id, memberId, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at) without token values.
8. Session status (active/expired) is determined by comparing expired_at to current server time.

Database Query:
SELECT id, multi_user_todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at
FROM multi_user_todo_app_member_sessions
WHERE id = :sessionId AND multi_user_todo_app_member_id = :userId

responseBody.description: Detailed session information including connection metadata and timestamps

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to retrieve
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Create a new todo item in the authenticated user's todo list.

This operation allows members to create new todo items with a title and optional fields including description, start date, and due date. Todos are created in incomplete state by default and appear in the user's active todo list immediately upon creation.

The title field is required and must not be empty. The description, start date, and due date fields are optional. If not provided, description defaults to an empty string and dates are set to null.

Every edit made to a todo (including this initial creation) is automatically recorded in the edit history table. Each edit history entry captures the before and after values of all modified fields, providing a complete audit trail of changes.

Authentication is required via Bearer token. Only authenticated members can create todos; guests cannot access this endpoint.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into multi_user_todo_app_todos table.

1. Validate authentication: Verify Bearer token in Authorization header belongs to a member (not guest)
2. Validate request body:
   - title: required, non-empty string
   - description: optional, can be empty string or omitted (default to empty string)
   - startDate: optional ISO date string or omitted
   - dueDate: optional ISO date string or omitted
3. Set isCompleted to false (default incomplete state)
4. Generate unique UUID for id field
5. Set createdAt and updatedAt to current timestamp (UTC)
6. Insert record into multi_user_todo_app_todos table
7. Create initial EditHistoryEntry record in multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table:
   - Reference the newly created todo by id
   - Store oldTitle as null, newTitle as provided title
   - Store oldDescription as null, newDescription as provided description
   - Store oldStartDate as null, newStartDate as provided startDate
   - Store oldDueDate as null, newDueDate as provided dueDate
   - Set editedAt to current timestamp
8. Return the full created todo object with all fields including id, createdAt, updatedAt

Error handling:
- Return 401 if authentication token is invalid or expired
- Return 403 if user is a guest (not authenticated member)
- Return 400 if title is missing or empty
- Return 400 if required validation fails

responseBody.description: The newly created todo with all fields

requestBody.description: Creation data for the new todo item

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation provides advanced list browsing capabilities for the user's private todo list. It supports filtering by completion status (active, completed, or all todos) and flexible sorting options based on creation date, start date, or due date. The response includes paginated results with metadata for navigating large result sets.

Each todo in the response contains essential information including title, description, date fields, and completion status. Users can only view their own todos—privacy and ownership boundaries are strictly enforced through user_id matching.

The endpoint handles null values in optional date fields (start_date and due_date) with special sorting behavior: when sorting by these fields, todos with missing dates appear last in the result set regardless of sort order.

Successful completion of a todo operation requires prior authentication. The user must provide a valid JWT token in the Authorization header. Unauthorized requests are rejected with appropriate error responses.

For detailed information about a single todo, use GET /todos/{id}. For creating new todos, use POST /todos. For editing existing todos, use PUT /todos/{id}. For viewing edit history, use GET /todos/{id}/history.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table filtered by user_id (current authenticated user) and deleted_at IS NULL (excluding trash items).

Apply filters:
- status filter: 'all' returns todos where deleted_at IS NULL, 'completed' filters where is_completed = true, 'incomplete' filters where is_completed = false

Apply pagination:
- Extract page and limit from requestBody
- Calculate offset as (page - 1) * limit
- Use LIMIT limit and OFFSET offset for database query

Apply sorting:
- sortBy parameter determines ORDER BY clause: 'createdAt' uses created_at, 'startDate' uses start_date, 'dueDate' uses due_date
- sortOrder determines direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending
- For start_date and due_date sorting, use COALESCE to handle NULL values: ORDER BY CASE WHEN start_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, start_date DESC
- Default sorting is by created_at descending

Return paginated response with:
- items array containing Todo.ISummary objects
- totalCount: count of matching records (for pagination metadata)
- page, limit: pagination parameters from request

Error handling:
- Throw NotFound if user_id does not match current user
- Throw ValidationError for invalid page (min 1), limit (1-100), status values, sortBy values, or sortOrder values

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo items with metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo by its unique identifier from the authenticated member's todo list.

This operation returns complete todo information including the todo's title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and timestamps. The todo must exist in the user's account and belong to the authenticated member for the request to succeed.

The system enforces strict privacy and ownership boundaries - users can only view their own todos. Any attempt to access another user's todo by ID will be rejected. The todo must exist in the database and be associated with the current user's account.

This operation is typically used when a user clicks on a specific todo from their todo list to view or edit its details. It requires the authenticated member to provide a valid JWT token in the Authorization header.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table for a todo with the specified ID.

1. Extract JWT token from Authorization header and validate authentication
2. Resolve the member_id from the authenticated token
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND member_id = {authenticated_member_id}
4. If no todo found, return 404 Not Found error
5. Return todo data with all fields: id, title, description, startDate, dueDate, isCompleted, createdAt, updatedAt
6. Do not return any todos that don't belong to the authenticated member

Error handling:
- 404 if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user
- 401 if no valid authentication token provided

Data transformation:
- Convert database record to Todo response object
- Ensure null dates are represented as null (not empty strings)
- Maintain ISO 8601 datetime format for dates

responseBody.description: Complete todo information with all fields

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to retrieve
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Update an existing todo in the authenticated member's todo list.

This operation modifies one or more fields of a todo belonging to the current member. The todo must exist in the member's account and belong to the current authenticated user. The system validates ownership for every update operation by checking that the todo is associated with the member's account.

Every update automatically creates an EditHistoryEntry record that tracks which fields changed and their previous values. This audit trail is preserved even when the todo is moved to trash or deleted. The edit history provides a complete chronology of changes to the todo throughout its lifecycle.

The title field cannot be updated to an empty string if provided. Description, start date, and due date can be updated to any valid value including null. The isCompleted field cannot be modified through this operation; use the toggle completion endpoint instead.

Related operations include GET /todos/{todoId} to retrieve current todo information, PATCH /todos/{todoId}/complete to toggle completion status, and GET /todos/{todoId}/history to view the edit history for this todo.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Verify the current user is authenticated as a member (not guest)
2. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table for record with id = todoId
3. Verify ownership: todo.user_id must match current member's id
4. Validate request body:
   - If title is provided, it must not be empty (non-zero length)
   - startDate and dueDate must be valid ISO 8601 date strings if provided
5. Build update set from provided fields (title, description, startDate, dueDate)
6. Perform UPDATE on multi_user_todo_app_todos table with new values
7. Update updatedAt timestamp to current time
8. Create EditHistoryEntry record in multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories:
   - Store old values from before update
   - Store new values from update request
   - Set editedAt to current time
   - Only record fields that actually changed
9. Return the updated todo record with all fields including new updatedAt value

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: return 404 Not Found
- Todo belongs to different user: return 403 Forbidden
- Title is empty string: return 400 Bad Request

responseBody.description: The updated todo object with all current field values including the new updatedAt timestamp

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to update
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Partial todo data containing any fields to update. All fields are optional, but at least one must be provided.

operations.description:
Toggles a todo's completion status between complete and incomplete.

This operation allows users to mark a todo as complete or mark a completed todo as incomplete. The toggle is a simple state change with no additional validation conditions beyond ownership verification.

When the completion status is toggled, the system automatically creates an EditHistoryEntry to record the change. This provides an audit trail of all status modifications per the edit history tracking requirements.

Only authenticated members can toggle the status of todos that belong to their account. The system validates that the todo exists in the user's account before performing the toggle operation.

The response includes the updated todo with the new isCompleted status and the updated timestamp.
operations.name: complete
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request - verify member JWT token
2. Extract todoId from path parameter
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for the todo record
4. Validate: todo exists AND todo.memberId equals the authenticated member's ID
5. If validation fails, return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden
6. Toggle isCompleted field: if true then false, if false then true
7. Update updatedAt timestamp to current UTC datetime
8. Insert new record into multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories with:
   - todoId: the todo ID
   - editedAt: current UTC datetime
   - Track old vs new isCompleted values in appropriate fields
9. Return updated todo record with new isCompleted and updatedAt values

Edge cases:
- Todo does not exist: return 404
- Todo belongs to another member: return 403 Forbidden
- Concurrent updates: use database transaction or optimistic locking

responseBody.description: Updated todo with the new completion status

parameters.description: Identifier of the todo whose completion status should be toggled
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before its completion status can be toggled

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to the trash.

This operation permanently removes a todo from the active todo list by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current datetime. The todo remains in the system and can be viewed in the trash, restored, or permanently deleted.

The operation enforces strict ownership validation - users can only delete their own todos. Any attempt to delete another user's todo is rejected with an authorization error.

The todo's edit history entries remain intact during soft deletion. They are only permanently removed when the todo is permanently deleted from the trash using the trash deletion endpoint.

Related operations:
- GET /todos/{todoId}: View todo details before deletion
- GET /todos/trash: View deleted todos in trash
- PUT /todos/{todoId}/restore: Restore a deleted todo back to the active list
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} (permanent): Permanently delete from trash (also deletes edit history)
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - require valid member session token
2. Extract todoId from path parameter (UUID format)
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for record matching todoId AND user_id = authenticated user's ID
4. If record not found, return 404 Not Found
5. Check if deleted_at is already non-null - if todo is already in trash, return 409 Conflict
6. Set deleted_at to current UTC timestamp
7. Update updated_at to current UTC timestamp
8. Commit transaction
9. Return 200 OK with the deleted todo object including deletedAt timestamp

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid authentication token provided
- 404 Not Found: Todo does not exist or belongs to another user
- 409 Conflict: Todo is already deleted (in trash)
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Invalid todoId format

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to delete
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of deleted todos (trash) belonging to the authenticated member.

This endpoint provides access to todos that have been soft-deleted by the user. Deleted todos are stored in a trash area where they remain visible to the owner but hidden from the normal todo list. Users can restore deleted todos from this location or permanently remove them.

The response includes only essential fields for trash display: the todo identifier, title, description, and the timestamp when the todo was deleted. Pagination is supported to efficiently handle large numbers of deleted todos.

Important: Users can only view their own deleted todos. The system enforces strict data isolation by filtering results to only include todos where user_id matches the authenticated member's ID.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table filtered by deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND user_id = current_auth_user_id. Apply pagination with configurable page number and limit. Return only essential fields: id, title, description, and deletedAt timestamp. Sort by deleted_at descending (newest deletions first) by default. The authenticated member can only view their own deleted todos.

Pagination parameters:
- page: current page number (default 1, minimum 1)
- limit: items per page (default 10, maximum 100)

Security: Always filter by user_id to enforce data isolation. Never return todos belonging to other users.

Error handling: Return 404 if no deleted todos exist for the user. No query parameters for filtering by status or date range for trash - trash only contains deleted items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from trash back to the active todo list.

This operation reverses a soft delete by moving the specified todo from the trash collection back to the normal todo list. The todo's deletedAt timestamp is cleared, and it immediately becomes visible in the user's active todo list.

The restoring user must be the owner of the todo. The system validates that the todo exists in the trash (has a deletedAt timestamp) before performing the restoration. This prevents attempting to restore todos that have already been restored or permanently deleted.

When a todo is restored, all of its original data is preserved including:
- Title and description
- Start date and due date
- Completion status (isCompleted)
- Creation timestamp (createdAt)
- Complete edit history from previous states

The restored todo can then be edited, completed, deleted again, or have its edit history viewed just like any other active todo.

Related operations:
- GET /api/todos/trash - View all deleted todos before restoration
- GET /api/todos/{id} - View the restored todo in its active state
- DELETE /api/todos/{id} - Soft delete a todo to move it to trash
- DELETE /api/todos/{id} - Permanent deletion from trash (also deletes edit history)
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Implement todo restoration from trash by:

1. Extract todoId from path parameter
2. Verify user is authenticated (member actor)
3. Query multi_user_todo_app_todos for the todo with id = todoId
4. Validate todo exists and is owned by the authenticated user
5. Check todo is in trash (deletedAt is not null)
6. If todo not in trash or not owned by user, return 404 Not Found
7. Update the todo by setting deletedAt to null/undefined
8. Query the updated todo record to return full details
9. Return the restored todo with all fields

Error handling:
- 404 when todoId does not exist or does not belong to user
- 404 when todo is not in trash (already restored or permanently deleted)
- 401 when user is not authenticated

Database operations:
- Single UPDATE query on multi_user_todo_app_todos
- No new edit history entries created on restoration
- Edit history remains intact and accessible via GET /api/todos/{id}/history

responseBody.description: The fully restored todo with all fields intact

parameters.description: The ID of the todo to restore from trash
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete edit history for a specific todo.

This endpoint returns all edit history entries associated with the identified todo, sorted by edit timestamp in descending order (most recent changes first). Each history entry captures the state of fields before and after an edit, documenting what was changed during each modification.

The edit history provides an audit trail of all modifications made to the todo's title, description, start date, and due date fields. Users can view this history to track changes over time and understand how their todo has evolved.

Only the owner of the todo can access its edit history. This enforces data privacy and ensures users can only view changes to their own todos.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table for all entries where todo_id matches the path parameter todoId.
Filter entries by ownership - only return history for todos owned by the authenticated member.
Join with multi_user_todo_app_todos to verify ownership via member_id relationship.
Order results by edited_at descending (most recent first).
Return paginated results with totalCount for cursor-based navigation.
Each response entry includes: id, editedAt timestamp, and old/new values for title, description, startDate, dueDate fields that were changed in that edit.
Handle UUID validation for todoId path parameter.
Return 404 if todo does not exist or user does not own the todo.
Return 401 if not authenticated.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of edit history entries for the todo

parameters.description: Identifier of the todo whose edit history to retrieve
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash, including all associated edit history entries.

This operation removes a todo from the system entirely when it exists in the trash (soft-deleted state). The todo will no longer be accessible through any API endpoint and cannot be recovered after this operation completes.

Before deleting the todo, the system verifies that the todo belongs to the authenticated user and is currently in the trash (has a deleted_at timestamp). The operation then deletes all edit history entries associated with the todo from the edit history table to ensure complete data removal.

Only the owner of the todo can perform this operation. Users cannot permanently delete todos that belong to other users or todos that have not been soft-deleted first (those must be moved to trash before permanent deletion).
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify authentication token is present in Authorization header.

Query multi_user_todo_app_todos table by id matching {todoId} parameter.

Validate that the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user (member actor) by checking user_id foreign key.

Validate that the todo is in trash state by checking deleted_at column is not null.

Query multi_user_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table for all entries where todo_id matches the todo being deleted.

Execute database transaction:
  1. Delete all edit history entries for this todo (cascade delete not sufficient per business rules)
  2. Delete the todo record from multi_user_todo_app_todos

Commit transaction and return success response.

Rollback transaction if any error occurs during deletion.

Handle edge cases:
  - Todo not found: return 404 error
  - Todo not owned by authenticated user: return 403 error
  - Todo not in trash (deleted_at is null): return 400 error indicating todo must be soft-deleted first

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
